toc.title: Block, file and object storage, performance and hybrid options

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Tell block, file and object storage apart, and match each to a use case
  • Choose the right EBS volume type for IOPS or throughput
  • Choose among EFS and the FSx family for shared file storage
  • Tune S3 for request rate and latency
  • Use Storage Gateway for hybrid storage

2Block, file and object storage, performance and hybrid options

Running case

Lantern and Loom Speeds Up Storage

  • A database needs steady, high IOPS
  • Web servers in several zones must share one file area
  • Artists on Windows want ordinary file shares
  • Product images keep growing, and traffic is spiky
  • The warehouse systems need a bridge to cloud storage
  • Your job: pick the storage type that fits each need

Block, File and Object Storage

  • Block (EBS, instance store): a disk for one instance, in one AZ; databases, boot volumes, low-latency I/O
  • File (EFS, FSx): a shared file system many servers mount; shared content, home directories, lift and shift
  • Object (S3): objects by key over an API; images, backups, data lakes, static content

Exam tip: One server and a disk: block. Many servers sharing files: file. Internet-scale objects: S3.

Amazon EBS Volume Types [Verify live]

Volume Class Best for Notable limits
gp3 General Purpose SSD Most workloads, boot volumes, small databases Up to 80,000 IOPS, 2,000 MiB/s
gp2 General Purpose SSD Older default Up to 16,000 IOPS
io2 Block Express Provisioned IOPS SSD Sub-millisecond, more than 80,000 IOPS, 99.999% durability Up to 256,000 IOPS
io1 Provisioned IOPS SSD I/O-intensive databases Up to 64,000 IOPS
st1 Throughput HDD Big data, logs, streaming 500 MiB/s, not bootable
sc1 Cold HDD Infrequent access, lowest cost 250 MiB/s, not bootable
  • As of 5 November 2026: limits keep rising; check the page

Exam tip: IOPS-heavy: SSD. Throughput-heavy: HDD. Beyond gp3: Provisioned IOPS.

EBS Features and Instance Store

  • An EBS volume lives in one Availability Zone; use snapshots to copy it elsewhere
  • Multi-Attach (io1, io2) lets several instances use one volume
  • Use EBS-optimized instances to reach the provisioned IOPS
  • You can change size, type and IOPS of a volume while it is in use
  • Instance store is disk on the host: very fast, but temporary
  • Instance store data is lost when the instance stops or terminates: use it for caches, buffers and scratch data

Exam tip: Data that must survive: EBS. Fast scratch space that can be lost: instance store.

Amazon EFS

  • Serverless, elastic NFS file storage that grows and shrinks automatically, to petabytes
  • Thousands of clients can mount it at once: EC2, containers and Lambda
  • Regional file systems store data across multiple AZs; One Zone uses a single AZ
  • Performance mode: General Purpose (the default and recommended)
  • Throughput mode: Elastic for spiky workloads, Provisioned for known needs, Bursting that scales with size
  • Linux only: Windows instances are not supported

Exam tip: Shared Linux files across servers and zones: EFS with Elastic throughput.

Amazon FSx File Systems

File system Protocol and strength Choose it for
FSx for Windows File Server SMB, Active Directory, native Windows features Windows shares and applications
FSx for Lustre A parallel file system with high throughput and S3 integration HPC, machine learning, media processing
FSx for NetApp ONTAP NFS, SMB and iSCSI, NetApp data management Multi-protocol and NetApp migrations
FSx for OpenZFS NFS, snapshots and clones Moving ZFS workloads

Exam tip: Windows and Active Directory: FSx for Windows. Fast parallel compute: FSx for Lustre.

Amazon S3 Performance [Verify live]

  • At least 3,500 write and 5,500 read requests per second per prefix; add prefixes and parallel connections
  • Multipart upload and byte-range fetches speed up large objects
  • Transfer Acceleration speeds long-distance transfers over the CloudFront edge network
  • CloudFront or ElastiCache speed up repeat reads
  • S3 Express One Zone: single-digit millisecond access, in one AZ
  • As of 5 November 2026: check current request rates

Exam tip: More requests per second: more prefixes and parallelism. Lowest latency: Express One Zone.

Hybrid Storage with AWS Storage Gateway [Verify live]

Gateway Presents Stores in AWS
S3 File Gateway NFS or SMB file shares Objects in S3, with a local cache
FSx File Gateway SMB access to FSx for Windows A FSx for Windows file system
Volume Gateway iSCSI block volumes Cached or stored volumes, with snapshots
Tape Gateway A virtual tape library Archive in S3
  • As of 5 November 2026: check whether FSx File Gateway is open to new customers

Exam tip: On-premises apps that need S3 as files: S3 File Gateway.

Choosing Storage

Need Choice
Database volume, steady IOPS EBS gp3, or io2 above 80,000 IOPS
Shared Linux files across AZs EFS
Windows shares with Active Directory FSx for Windows File Server
HPC scratch with S3 data FSx for Lustre
Internet-scale objects S3
Fastest object access S3 Express One Zone
Temporary host-local speed Instance store
On-premises apps using cloud storage Storage Gateway

Exam tip: Name the access method first: disk, shared files or objects.

What the Exam Asks: High-Performing Storage

  • Which storage type: block, file or object
  • Which EBS volume: gp3, io2, st1 or sc1
  • Which shared file system: EFS or one of the FSx family
  • Which S3 option: prefixes, Transfer Acceleration or Express One Zone
  • Which hybrid bridge: the Storage Gateway type

Exam tip: Underline the performance word: IOPS, throughput, latency or scale.

Design Check: Lantern and Loom Speeds Up Storage

Requirement Design
Database needs steady IOPS EBS gp3; io2 if beyond its limits
Web servers in three zones share files Amazon EFS
Artists need Windows file shares FSx for Windows File Server
Images grow without limit Amazon S3
Image processing needs single-digit millisecond access S3 Express One Zone
Warehouse systems need NFS to cloud storage S3 File Gateway
Throwaway scratch data Instance store
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

3Exam Q&A

3.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Lantern and Loom's order database needs sustained performance of 100,000 IOPS with consistent sub-millisecond latency. Which EBS volume type fits?

  • AGeneral Purpose SSD (gp2) with burst credits
  • BProvisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express)
  • CThroughput Optimized HDD (st1) volumes
  • DCold HDD (sc1) for infrequent access
Show the answer

Answer: B. io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS with sub-millisecond latency, beyond what the general purpose volumes and HDD volumes offer. HDD volumes are for throughput and cold data.

S2Linux web servers in three Availability Zones must read and write the same set of files, and the capacity should grow automatically. Which storage fits?

  • AAn EBS volume attached to each server
  • BInstance store on each server
  • CAn S3 bucket mounted as a local disk with no caching
  • DAmazon EFS, mounted by all the servers across the zones
Show the answer

Answer: D. EFS is a shared, elastic NFS file system that many servers across zones mount at the same time. EBS volumes and instance store belong to one server, and S3 is object storage.

S3The design team at Lantern and Loom needs Windows file shares that use their Active Directory sign-in. Which service fits?

  • AAmazon FSx for Windows File Server
  • BAmazon EFS with POSIX permissions
  • CAmazon EBS Multi-Attach on shared volumes
  • DAWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway as a share
Show the answer

Answer: A. FSx for Windows File Server provides native SMB file shares that join Active Directory. EFS does not support Windows instances, Multi-Attach is block storage, and Tape Gateway is for archive.

S4Which TWO statements about Amazon S3 request performance are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AS3 supports at least 3,500 write and 5,500 read requests per second per prefix
  • BA bucket is limited to a single prefix
  • CSpreading objects across several prefixes and parallelizing requests increases the total request rate
  • DCapacity and request rates must be provisioned in advance
  • ETransfer Acceleration lowers latency for clients in the same Region as the bucket
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. S3 scales automatically per prefix, and more prefixes with parallel requests multiply the rate. A bucket can have many prefixes, nothing is provisioned, and Transfer Acceleration helps long-distance transfers.

S5Warehouse applications on premises write files over NFS and need the data stored durably in Amazon S3, with a local cache for fast reads. Which service should the architect use?

  • AAWS Direct Connect with a private virtual interface
  • BAmazon EFS with a VPC mount target
  • CAWS Storage Gateway S3 File Gateway
  • DAmazon CloudFront with a custom origin
Show the answer

Answer: C. S3 File Gateway presents NFS or SMB file shares on premises and stores the files as S3 objects, with a local cache. Direct Connect is a network link, EFS is a cloud file system, and CloudFront is a CDN.

4Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Block, file, object EBS, EFS and FSx, S3
EBS SSD for IOPS, HDD for throughput; io2 for the highest IOPS; one AZ
Shared files EFS for Linux, FSx for Windows, Lustre, ONTAP and OpenZFS

Hybrid Storage Gateway bridges on-premises and AWS
